Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 72, verse 1–3:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened and said, 'Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to righteousness, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.' And [they said], 'Exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has not taken a companion or a son.'"﴾

His majesty, glorified is His praise, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, "Allah has revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened" to this Qur'an, ﴿and said﴾ to their people when they heard it: ﴿"Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to righteousness"﴾, meaning: it points to the truth and the path of what is correct. ﴿"So we have believed in it"﴾, meaning: we have affirmed it. ﴿"And we will never associate anyone with our Lord"﴾, meaning: anyone of His creation.

The cause of this group of jinn listening to the Qur'an was as follows:

As reported:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar related to me, saying: Abu Hisham, meaning al-Makhzumi, related to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) neither recited to the jinn nor saw them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out with a group of his companions, intending the market of 'Ukaz. He said: The devils had been prevented from eavesdropping on news of the heavens, and shooting stars were sent against them, so the devils returned to their people. They said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "We have been barred from news of the heavens, and shooting stars have been sent against us." They said: "Nothing has prevented you from news of the heavens except that something has happened."

He said: So they set out, striking the eastern and western regions of the earth, seeking out what this thing was that had happened. He said: They went striking the eastern and western regions of the earth, tracing what it was that had come between them and news of the heavens. He said: The group who headed toward Tihamah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Nakhlah, while he was intending the market of 'Ukaz and was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. He said: When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "By Allah, this is what came between you and news of the heavens." He said: Then, when they returned to their people, they said: "O our people, ﴿Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to righteousness, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.﴾" He said: Then Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened"﴾, and what was revealed to him was only the statement of the jinn.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from 'Asim, from Warqa', who said: The delegation of Zawba'ah and his companions came to Mecca to the Prophet (ﷺ), heard the Prophet's (ﷺ) recitation, then departed. That is His statement: ﴿And when We turned toward you a group of the jinn listening to the Qur'an, and when they were present they said, "Be silent."﴾ He said: They were nine, among them Zawba'ah.

⁕ I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His statement: ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened"﴾ — it is the statement of Allah: ﴿And when We turned toward you a group of the jinn﴾. The heaven was not guarded during the interval between 'Isa and Muhammad. So when Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ), the lowest heaven was guarded, and the devils were struck with shooting stars. Iblis said: "Something has happened on the earth," so he commanded the jinn, and they dispersed across the earth to bring him news of what had happened. The first to be dispatched was a group from the people of Nasibin, which is a land in Yemen; they were the nobles and leaders of the jinn. He sent them to Tihamah and the region adjoining Yemen. Those men went on until they came to the valley of Nakhlah, which is two nights' journey from the [Yemen]. There they found the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) praying the morning prayer, and they heard him reciting the Qur'an. When they came to him, they said: "Listen attentively." When it was concluded, meaning when he had finished the prayer, they turned back to their people as warners, meaning as believers. The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) had not known of them nor perceived that they had been turned toward him, until Allah revealed to him: ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened."﴾

* *

As for His statement: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord"﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is: "So we believed in it and will never associate anyone with our Lord, and we believe that the command of our Lord, His authority and His power are exalted."

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His statement: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord"﴾: He means His deed, His command and His power.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His statement: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord"﴾: He means: exalted is the command of our Lord.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah, concerning this verse: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: the command of our Lord.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: the command of our Lord.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His statement: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has not taken a companion or a son﴾: "His command is exalted, that He should take [one] — and it is not what they claimed — a companion or a son." And he recited: ﴿Say, "He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, nor is there to Him any equivalent."﴾ He said: That does not occur from Him.

Others said: What is meant by it is the majesty of our Lord and His remembrance.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, who said: 'Ikrimah said, concerning His statement: ﴿the majesty of our Lord﴾: the majesty of our Lord.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: Khalid ibn Yazid related to me, saying: Abu Isra'il related to us, from Fudayl, from Mujahid, concerning His statement: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord"﴾: the majesty of our Lord.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Taymi, who said: 'Ikrimah said: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: the majesty of our Lord.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His statement: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord"﴾: that is, exalted is His majesty, His greatness and His command.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning His statement: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: "Exalted is the command of our Lord": His greatness is exalted.

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: exalted is the wealth of our Lord.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, from his father, who said: al-Hasan said, concerning His statement: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: "the wealth of our Lord."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from al-Hasan: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: "the wealth of our Lord."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His statement: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: "the wealth of our Lord."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah, concerning the word of Allah: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord"﴾: one of them said: "His wealth," and the other said: "His greatness."

Others said: What is meant by it is the *jadd* which is the grandfather of the father; they said: that was from the speech of ignorant jinn.

Those who said this:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Sarah related to me, from his father, from Abu Ja'far: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: it was a statement from the ignorant jinn.

Others said: What is meant by it is: His remembrance.

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the word of Allah: ﴿Exalted is the majesty of our Lord﴾: "His remembrance."

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the view of those who said: what is meant is: exalted is the greatness of our Lord, His power and His authority.

We said that this is more correct because *jadd* in the speech of the Arabs has two meanings. One is the *jadd* which is the grandfather of the father or the grandfather of the mother, and it is not permissible to attribute this to these men whom Allah described with this description, for they have said: ﴿So we believed in it and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.﴾ Whoever attributes to Allah a son, or a grandfather, or says that He is a father of a father or a father of a mother, there is no doubt that he is among the polytheists.

The other meaning is *jadd* meaning good fortune (*hazz*). It is said: "So-and-so has *jadd* in this matter" when he has a share in it, and this is what is called in Persian *bakht* (fortune). This is the meaning intended by this group of jinn in their saying: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord"﴾, God willing.

They only meant that His share of kingship, authority, power and greatness is lofty, so He has no companion or son; for a companion exists only for the weak and incapable one whom the driving desire compels to take one, and a son comes only from a desire that drives one to the intercourse from which a child results. So the group of jinn said: the kingdom, authority, power and greatness of our Lord are too exalted to be weak, with the weakness of His creatures who are compelled by desire to take a companion, or to have intercourse from which a son results.

The statement of Allah about them clarifies the correctness of what we have said: that they only declared Allah free of taking a companion or a son by His statement: ﴿And [they said], "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord; He has not taken a companion or a son."﴾ It is said from this: a man is *jaddi* and *jadid* and *majdud*, meaning one with good fortune in what he is in. From this is the saying of Hatim al-Ta'i:

*Raid the Banu Thu'l, for raiding is your jadd;*
*Count the hills, and do not weep for one who was slain.*

*Hatim's verse is attributed to him (Shu'ara' al-Nasraniyyah 128), and in it "hazzakum" stands in place of "jaddukum," and both have the same meaning. Its commentator said: al-rawabi means the nobles, or the origin and nobility. In Lisan al-'Arab (jadd) and in the revealed text: "Exalted is the majesty of our Lord" — it was said: its jadd is its greatness; it was also said: its wealth. Mujahid said: jadd of our Lord: the majesty of our Lord. Some said: the greatness of our Lord, and these two are nearly equivalent. End of quotation. These interpretations are suitable for interpreting the verse of Hatim: raiding is the might and greatness of the Arabs, the cause of their awe and majesty in the eyes of their enemies; their courage in war and combat is their share by which they were known in this world, refusing humiliation and disdaining the subjugation of kings and tyrants.*

Another said:

*May your jadd be raised; indeed I am a man whom the enemies have made to drink for you buckets in turn.*

*The author did not attribute this verse. It more closely resembles the verse of al-Hutay'ah in his rhyming ode addressed to our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, apologizing for his satire of al-Zibriqan ibn Badr al-Tamimi, whose opening line is: "Umamah has left you except for a question." I did not find it in the printed Diwan of al-Hutay'ah, nor in Jamharat Ash'ar al-'Arab (151–154). His saying "may your jadd be raised" means: he prays that Allah raise his good fortune and remembrance. "Sijal" is the plural of "sajl," a bucket; he apologizes for what the slanderers had plotted against him.*

* *

As for His statement: ﴿mā ittakhadha ṣāḥibatan﴾ (He has not taken a companion)

That means a wife. ﴿Wa lā waladan﴾ (nor a son).

The reciters differed in reading His statement: ﴿And that He, exalted is He﴾. Abu Ja'far the reciter and six other letters read it with a fatha: ﴿that He: a group of the jinn listened﴾, ﴿and that the mosques belong to Allah﴾, ﴿and that he used to say, our foolish one﴾, ﴿and that there were men of mankind﴾, ﴿and that when the servant of Allah stood calling Him﴾, ﴿and that if they had remained upon the way﴾. Nafi' used to read them with a kasra except three letters: the first is ﴿Say: it has been revealed to me that he: a group listened﴾, the second is ﴿and that if they had remained﴾, and the third is ﴿and that the mosques belong to Allah﴾. As for the reciters of Kufa other than 'Asim, they read with a fatha everything at the end of Surat al-Najm and the beginning of Surat al-Jinn except His statement ﴿so they said, "Indeed, we have heard"﴾, and His statement ﴿Say: I only call upon my Lord﴾ and what follows it to the end of the surah; and they read these with a kasra, other than His statement ﴿that he may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾. As for 'Asim, he read all of them with a kasra except His statement ﴿and that the mosques belong to Allah﴾, which he read with a fatha. As for Abu 'Amr, he read all of them with a kasra except His statement ﴿and that if they had remained upon the way﴾, which he read with a fatha, along with what follows it. Those who read all of them with a fatha except in the place of speech, such as ﴿so they said, "Indeed, we have heard"﴾ and ﴿Say: I only call upon my Lord﴾ and the like, joined "that" throughout the surah to His statement ﴿so we believed in it﴾, and "we believed in all of that," so they read it with a fatha by the occurrence of belief upon it. Al-Farra' used to say: Do not let it prevent you that you find belief disliked in some of these with a fatha; what is disliked with the manifestation of belief may be good in it when it is a present verb of belief. So it is required to read "that" with a fatha, as the Arabs said:

*When the adorned women appeared one day, and they arched their eyebrows and their eyes.*

*The verse has been cited previously in volume 27 (p. 176), and we explained it there at length, so refer back to it.*

So "the eyes" is in the accusative by following "the eyebrows," though eyebrows are not arched but darkened with kohl; so kohl is implied for them. Likewise, it is implied in the place where "we believed, we confirmed, and we witnessed" is not good. He said: Supporting the accusative reading is His statement ﴿and that if they had remained upon the way﴾, so whoever reads with a kasra should omit "an" from "law," because "an," when lightened, is not a quotation. Do you not see that you say: "I say, if you had done it, you would have done it," and you do not insert "an"? As for those who read all of them with a kasra, and they say ﴿and that if they had remained﴾, they seem to have implied an oath along with "law," and separated it from the continuation of the opening of the speech, so they said: "By Allah, if they had remained..." He said: The Arabs insert "an" in this position with the oath and delete it. The poet said:

*So I swear, if anything had come to us with His messenger other than you, but we did not find for you a refuge.*

*The verse is by Imru' al-Qays; it was cited previously in volumes 12 (p. 18) and 13 (p. 152), so refer back to them, for we explained it at length.*

They said: Another recited to us:

*Indeed, by Allah, if you were free, and you are not free nor a manumitted slave.*

*This verse is among the grammarians' evidence for the light "an" derived from the heavy, said by some to govern and by others not to govern (al-Insaf fi Masa'il al-Khilaf by Ibn al-Anbari, Cairo edition 1:126, without attribution). al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, citing the verse (folio 344): "The Arabs insert 'an' in this position with the oath, and delete it. The poet said: 'So I swear, if anything..' the verse. And another recited to me: 'By Allah, indeed..' the verse." The author has transmitted al-Farra's entire statement on opening and breaking the hamza of "an" in the verses of Surat al-Jinn, so we will not lengthen the discussion by transmitting it, and we suffice with this reference.*

He who read all of them with a kasra inserted "an" and put ﴿and that the mosques belong to Allah﴾ in the accusative; he restricted that to revelation, and considered ﴿and that if they had remained﴾ to have an implied oath in it, as I described. As for Nafi', what he read with a fatha he returned to His statement ﴿it has been revealed to me﴾, and what he read with a kasra he made part of the speech of the jinn. The reading I prefer is to recite with a fatha what is revelation and with a kasra what is the speech of the jinn, because that is the most eloquent in Arabic and the clearest in meaning, though the other readings have valid aspects whose soundness is not rejected.

He said: The devils had been prevented from eavesdropping on news of the heavens, and shooting stars were sent against them, so the devils returned to their people. They said: "What is the matter with you?" They said: "We have been barred from news of the heavens, and shooting stars have been sent against us." They said: "Nothing has prevented you from news of the heavens except that something has happened."

He said: So they set out, striking the eastern and western regions of the earth, seeking out what this thing was that had happened. He said: They went striking the eastern and western regions of the earth, tracing what it was that had come between them and news of the heavens. He said: The group who headed toward Tihamah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Nakhlah, while he was intending the market of 'Ukaz and was leading his companions in the dawn prayer. He said: When they heard the Qur'an, they listened to it and said: "By Allah, this is what came between you and news of the heavens." He said: Then, when they returned to their people, they said: "O our people, ﴿Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Qur'an, guiding to righteousness, so we have believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.﴾" He said: Then Allah revealed to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "It has been revealed to me that a group of the jinn listened"﴾, and what was revealed to him was only the statement of the jinn.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 72, verses 4–6:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And that the foolish one among us used to speak against Allah an outrageous lie (shatat)﴾ (4) ﴿And we thought that men and jinn would never speak a lie against Allah﴾ (5) ﴿And that there were men among mankind who used to seek refuge with men among the jinn, so they increased them in burden (rahaq)﴾ (6)

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And if they had remained upon the way, We would have given them abundant water to drink,﴾ ﴿that We might test them therein. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord – He will make him endure a punishing ascent.﴾

The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, recited it in the form of a statement, with an alif (qul innama ad'u, "I only call"). Whoever recites it thus takes it as a report from Allah about His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ that he said it. The meaning of the speech is then: when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they crowded around him, and he said to them: "I only call upon my Lord, and I associate none with Him." from His creation, if He intends something against me, and no helper can help me against Him.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning the Prophet ﷺ because some of the jinn said: "I will protect him."

Those who said this:

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, who said: a man from Hadramawt claimed that it had been mentioned to him that a jinni from their nobles, a follower, said: "Muhammad only wants us to protect him, and I will protect him." * *

He says: nor will I find, apart from Allah, a place of refuge to which I may flee.

As:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: "Say: I do not know whether what you are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a lengthy term" (25) "He is the Knower of the Unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone (26) except to a messenger whom He has approved; for indeed He sends before him and behind him guards (27) that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord. And He encompasses what is with them and has enumerated everything in number" (28).

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people: "I do not know whether what your Lord promises you of punishment and the establishment of the Hour is near," "or whether my Lord will appoint for it a lengthy term," meaning: a known limit whose duration will be long.

And His words: "He is the Knower of the Unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone except to a messenger whom He has approved."

By "the Knower of the Unseen" is meant the Knower of what is hidden from the sight of His creatures, so that they have not seen it. He does not reveal His unseen to anyone, so that they know it or He shows it to them, except a messenger whom He has approved; for He reveals to him of that what He wills.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similar to what we have said on this.
